chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ismail al-Sarraj, from Ibn Muskan, from Thabit ibn Sa'id who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Thabit! What have you to do with the people? Refrain from the people and do not invite anyone to your matter (al-Wilayah), for, by God, even if the people of the heavens and the people of the earths were to gather together to guide a servant whose straying God intends, they would not have the capability to guide him.
And even if the people of the heavens and the people of the earths were to gather to lead astray a servant whose guidance God intends, they would not have the capability to lead him astray.

Refrain from the people, and let no one say 'my uncle, my brother, the son of my uncle, and my neighbour', for when God intends good for a servant, He purifies his soul so that he does not hear good except that he recognises it, nor evil except that he rejects it. Then God casts a word into his heart by which He gathers his affair.'

key_terms.أَمْرِكُمْ: Your matter/cause — refers to al-Wilayah, the recognition of and allegiance to the Imamate
key_terms.ضَلَالَة: Straying, misguidance — divinely willed separation from the path
key_terms.طَيَّبَ رُوحَهُ: Purified his soul — God's action of preparing a person's spirit to receive good
key_terms.كَلِمَة: A word — a divine inspiration cast into the heart, uniting the believer's affairs

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about inviting people to the Wilayah and divine guidance?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) instructed his companion Thabit ibn Sa'id not to invite others to the cause of Wilayah (allegiance to the Imams), grounding this instruction in the absolute sovereignty of divine will over guidance and misguidance. The Imam employed the hyperbolic image of all creation failing to override God's decree — if God wills a person's straying or guidance, no collective effort of all heavenly and earthly beings can alter that. The teaching reflects the early Shia situation of taqiyyah (precautionary concealment), when openly proselytising for the Imamate in the Abbasid-era political climate was dangerous; the Imam advised discretion over zeal, trusting God to prepare hearts as He wills.
